segs: "Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God"
"All the prophets call Yisrael to teshuvah,
and he teaches them with what they should appease Him:
קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים וְשׁוּבוּ אֶל ה׳
'Take with you words and return to Hashem'"
certainly the essence of teshuvah and remorse
is alluded to in the holy Torah
however, there are several levels in teshuvah,
as is stated in the Gemara
"Here it is out of fear, here out of love" —
that out of fear, deliberate sins become like unintentional ones,
and out of love they become like merits.
And certainly the "here out of fear"
is meant as referring to fear of punishment alone,
is like the level of love.
Rather, it is meant in its plain sense:
that after the sin he regrets immediately;
and this is included in all the souls of Yisrael,
that they immediately have a thought of teshuvah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה הֶעָוֹן כְּשׁוֹגֵג.
and through this the sin becomes like an unintentional one.
between a deliberate sin and an unintentional one
the deliberate sinner does the deed
And when the deliberate sinner regrets in his thought
then the sin of the thought is erased,
and only the deed alone remains,
And for the actual deed of the sin itself
the four categories of atonement are needed,
as our Sages of blessed memory said
And likewise we find in the holy Torah,
in the episode of the Golden Calf,
that Moshe immediately asked for mercy:
that Yisrael immediately had thoughts of teshuvah;
for it had become like unintentional sins.
For that is why it says
"This people has sinned a great sin"
and the term chet denotes an unintentional sin;
only that it is "a great sin,"
which is the most severe of all,
and which moreover involves chillul Hashem,
even the unintentional sin is very severe.
"And on the day that I make account, I will account"
the rectifying of the actual deed of the sin;
and about this it says "and on the day that I make account":
that is, every year on Yom Kippur
it is accounted for and diminished,
and is erased little by little
from the deed of the sin,
and they will be as before the sin,
as at the time of Matan Torah,
when it was said about them
Let us return to our subject:
for behold, there in Hoshea it says
"for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
meaning that it has become like unintentional sins;
and this is the teshuvah that is always found,
אַמְנָם הֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר שָׁם גַּם כֵּן
as our Rabbis of blessed memory said
that it reaches up to the Throne of Glory.
And this is only for those who act lishmah,
as they of blessed memory said
"For Your kindness is great above the heavens"
And from what it says, "for you have stumbled,"
meaning it became like unintentional sins,
it is only out of fear of punishment,
so how can one reach, from this,
such that everything will be rectified?
"Then those who fear Hashem spoke together"
and also regarding Eliyahu and Elisha:
and "He spoke to me: This is the table," etc.
And by your taking words with you,
meaning the aspect of the Written Torah,
you will be able to return all the way to Hashem.
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that is, through toil in the Oral Torah,
which is called amirah, speech in a whisper,
at the meal of Shabbos night;
that it will be possible to rectify
עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
through toil in the Oral Torah,
that it is along the lines of what they said
"With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for with words of Torah";
so too, with teshuvah it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for with words of Torah.
And this is through the toil of the soul
each time, more and more, in words of Torah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְחֶה הֶעָוֹן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
and through this the sin is erased completely,
as they of blessed memory said
"For in much wisdom is much vexation"
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ יוֹתֵר רוֹב כַּעַס
that the more abundant anger there is
through the yetzer hara in the soul,
the more there will increase through this
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִתְקָן הָרוֹב כַּעַס.
through which the abundant anger will be rectified.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ ׳וְקַח טוֹב׳:
And about this it says afterwards "and take the good":
He will take good in its place;
and that is the Oral Torah,
for "there is no good but Torah"
"The Torah of Your mouth is good to me"
And it says "and let us render bulls with our lips":
and the other categories of atonement in actual deed
as they of blessed memory said
"This is the law of the burnt-offering," etc.
"Whoever engages in the law of the burnt-offering," etc.
And it says afterwards in the haftarah:
"Who is wise, that he may understand these things;
understanding, that he may know them," etc.
זֶה חוֹזֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁנִּזְכַּר לְמַעְלָה,
This refers back to what was mentioned above:
that the main rectification of all the blemishes
However, there is a further condition in the matter:
that a person should not take credit for himself,
גַּם אִם הוּא פּוֹנֶה אֶת עַצְמוֹ
to toil in words of Torah,
as though he has some advantage of his own.
"I will be as the dew to Yisrael"
that he should know in his soul
שֶׁגַּם כָּל כֹּחַ רוֹב חָכְמָה שֶׁלּוֹ
that even all the power of his abundant wisdom
הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׁפָּע לוֹ מִלְּעֵילָא,
is only what flows to him from Above,
like the matter of the dew,
which one does not see at all at the time it descends,
when one sees the moisture of the ground,
does one see that dew has fallen.
that you should know in your soul
that I bend Myself down to you
which, when the hand of the one receiving pulls it,
And this is "from Me is your fruit found":
that you should know in your soul
that you have brought forth in Torah —
in the manner of what they of blessed memory said
"that they did not let him produce fruit,"
and as is stated in Tanchuma Noach
"The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life"
יֵשׁ לְךָ פְּרִי יָפֶה מִן הַבָּנִים,
"You have a fruit finer than children,"
know that this fruit of yours too
"Who is wise, that he may understand these things":
that even one who engages in the wisdom of the Torah,
still needs understanding of the heart:
וְגַם אִם הוּא נָבוֹן בְּבִינַת הַלֵּב,
and even if he is understanding with understanding of the heart,
that is, to join the wisdom in his mind
with the will in his heart,
because this is the main intent
"For the ways of Hashem are straight," etc.:
because even in engagement in Torah
"for those who go to its right, it is an elixir of life,
and for those who go to its left," etc.
to know that "from Me is your fruit found."
And the end of the haftarah
"And you shall eat plenty and be satisfied," etc.,
and My people shall never be ashamed"
and My people shall never be ashamed"
And well known regarding this is
that one sent his son to receive a blessing,
and the sage said to him:
"May you not be shamed and may you not be ashamed."
the Holy One, blessed be He, blessed Yisrael,
"and they shall not be ashamed" mentioned above.
that he blessed him not to be shamed by people,
that it was a small thing in his eyes,
since he was not concerned about this.
that it is a great thing:
מָה דִּבְרִיךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
the blessing with which the Holy One, blessed be He, blessed Yisrael,
And it is an allusion to
through engagement and toil in Torah,
for which the ways of teshuvah are closed off,
And about this it says "and you shall eat plenty":
that is, in engagement in Torah,
and as they of blessed memory said
the verse speaks of words of Torah."
And this is what it says, "and be satisfied":
that he should satiate himself with words of Torah,
as our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded
"And he shall rest satisfied; he shall not be visited by evil"
"And you shall praise the Name of Hashem your God
who has dealt wondrously with you":
one, the sense of explicit revelation,
as they of blessed memory said
and "a minor who knows how to express explicitly"
And the term pele also indicates
"Behold, I will again do wondrously," etc.,
"and the understanding of its men of understanding shall be hidden"
And this is the meaning of
as to the way of their rectification —
"and My people shall never be ashamed":
that is, that he will not be ashamed in himself
because of the greatness of the blemish,
to lift up my face to You, my God"
"And you shall know that I am in the midst of Yisrael," etc.:
this is the matter of the second condition
that he should know this in his soul,
that even his toil in engagement in Torah
comes about through a Divine power
וְאֵין עוֹד שׁוּם יִתְרוֹן בָּזֶה מִצִּידוֹ.
and there is no further advantage in this from his own side.
for everything will be rectified completely,
It is stated in the Gemara, Yoma
for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,
'Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God'"
why it needed to bring a proof from the Prophets,
when this very expression is found
in the holy Torah as well,
"And you shall return unto Hashem your God," etc.
"and you shall listen to His voice."
For the meaning of "unto Hashem your God"
is that this is the essence of teshuvah:
regarding the fact that there has become distant from a person's heart
the holy Name Havayah, blessed be He.
For this is the essence and foundation of everything:
that this belief be fixed in the soul,
that Havayah, blessed be He, is Elokim.
whose meaning is that He is mighty and all-capable
this is easy for a person's heart
But the aspect of the Name Havayah,
and is Master of all the forces,
and all the forces are nothing apart from Him,
who was, is, and will be,
וְאַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
and "You were the same before the world was created,
and You are the same since the world was created" —
it is hard for this to become fixed
because he sees the opposite appearance.
And for this reason the first utterance
which is the general principle of the entire Torah:
that this belief be fixed in the heart,
"Know this day and lay it to your heart
And at the time of Matan Torah
this became fixed with clear knowledge,
perceptibly, in all the souls of Yisrael;
and as they of blessed memory said
the utterance 'I am Hashem your God,'
the words of Torah became fixed in their hearts."
וְגַם אַחַר זֶה נִיתַּן כָּל הַתּוֹרָה
And also after this the whole Torah was given
as six hundred and thirteen counsels,
and become distant, in hester panim,
from His providence, blessed be He —
for him it is extremely hard
to fix this belief in his soul,
since he has inclined in his deeds
toward the aspect opposite to this.
"and you shall return unto Hashem your God,"
"and you shall listen to His voice":
that is, through hearing the voice
there will return to his soul
namely through the six hundred and thirteen counsels,
However, in Hoshea it says without qualification
"Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God":
it is possible to reach back again
to the aspect of "Hashem your God"
from the depths of the heart,
as is stated in the holy Zohar
for in one hour, in one moment,
they are close to the Holy One, blessed be He."
Therefore the Gemara cited above brings
the proof that great is teshuvah,
for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,
that is, that through teshuvah alone
one can reach up to the Throne of Glory,
meaning to the aspect of "Hashem your God";
and this is learned specifically from Hoshea,
Hashem is my shepherd; I shall not lack"
That is, when this becomes clear
that Hashem Yisbarach, who brings everything into being,
is the One who shepherds him,
then of itself he lacks nothing.
"though I walk, etc., I will not fear"
because it is clear before me
that even there "You are with me,"
that this too was from His providence, blessed be He.
For "Your rod and Your staff — they comfort me":
that through the rod of chastisement
is from His providence, blessed be He.
And this itself becomes a staff to comfort him,
"And you shall return unto Hashem your God"
there becomes known in his soul
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הוּא בַּעַל הַכּוֹחוֹת כּוּלָּם
that the Name Havayah is Master of all the forces,
and oversees and brings into being all the forces.
for it to become known in his soul
that the Name Havayah is "your God,"
And to this our Sages alluded
regarding the manna, which is called "white":
because it whitens the sins of Yisrael;
and Rashi of blessed memory explained
they would subjugate their hearts to the Omnipresent.
it is stated in the Gemara
thus they were found directing their hearts to the Omnipresent."
Here it is stated in the language of "directing."
"'And it came to pass, when Moshe raised his hand'
do the hands of Moshe, etc.?
Rather, when Yisrael would look upward
And likewise with the copper serpent:
And in truth the meaning is
as is stated in the Bartenura
regarding the juxtaposition of the mishnah,
which speaks above of the intention of the heart.
And why did it change to the language of "subjugating"?
of after the soul had already been touched
by the aspect of opposition and distance
from the serpent and from Amalek;
to subjugate one's heart to the Omnipresent
in which one had already become distant.
that it whitens the sins of Yisrael,
and Rashi explained in the language of "subjugating":
out of the state of distance,
through this their sins were whitened
they shall be white as snow"
